newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian shares rise in active trade.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian shares rise in active trade.

text.p: Shares ended generally higher in active Tuesday trade at the Nigerian stock exchange, dealers said.
The all-share index closed at 6,146.99 from 6,140.95 on Friday, the last day on which the index was published.
Construction firm G. Cappa gained almost five percent following the listing of some 40 million new shares offered in a recent rights issue. It closed 21 kobo higher at 4.46 naira.
Conglomerate PZ industries which advanced 65 kobo to 32.50 naira.
Unipetrol went up by 50 kobo to 34.00 naira. African Petroleum, National Oil and Texaco were all 10 kobo up respectively at 27.85 naira, 26.90 naira and 23.35 naira.
Cadbury rose 10 kobo to 23.20 naira and Union Dicon Salt advanced 12 kobo to 31.62 naira.
Insurance shares continued their strong performance. AIICO went five kobo up to 5.40 naira, the same amount as Presitge Assurance which closed at 4.65 naira.
Cement Company of Northern Nigeria gained six kobo to 2.96 naira.
Benue Cement Company gained five kobo to end at 3.73 naira, Ashaka Cement was five kobo higher at 14.85 naira.
Union Bank was 10 kobo up at 6.70 naira. Traders said the good recent performance had had a spin-off effect for some of the smaller banks.
Lion Bank and Trade Bank added one kobo each to close at 58 kobo and 1.43 naira respectively, while Trans International Bank closed two kobo higher at 1.08 naira.
Paint makers' shares suffered with many on offer and few takers. Berger Paints slid 10 kobo to 5.70 naira and CAP plc fell two kobo to 8.58 naira.
Further sales of CFAO forced its shares to also close seven kobo down at 5.85 naira and Nigerian Yeast and Alcohol Manufacturing Company dropped two kobo to 6.75 naira.
Two deals worth 104.8 million naira were done in gilts.
One was in a development stock maturing in 2011 with a 12.5 percent coupon rate valued at 93.8 million naira. The other, worth 11 million naira, was in a paper maturing in 13 years at 12.5 percent.
